messages:
matt: Heads up — after the 4872 merge I'm seeing a p95 decode latency plateau on canary and a CI perf job failure. spike started ~0900 UTC. logs below.

matt: CI job: runtime/perf/e2e-p95 — FAILED
matt: p95 before: 42ms -> after: 118ms (same traffic profile)

priya: :eyes: do we have a quick bisect candidate? any obvious diffs in scheduler/batcher heuristics in that PR?

matt: 4872 touched batcher threshold logic + warmup affinity routing. suspect flip in the adaptive microbatch threshold that increases small-batch tail.

dan: I ran a quick local bisect on a small repro. pointing at commit 9f2ab4e (batcher: prefer_warm_affinity=true default). reverting that locally drops p95 back to ~45ms.

liu: interesting — my flamegraphs from the perf CI run show a big increase in time in decode path, specifically attention transpose kernel calls. before the merge, GPU kernels were ~60% matmul, now attention-transpose is ~72% and stalls at kernel selection boundary.

kira: also seeing elevated KV cache eviction rates in canary metrics — prefix hitrate went from 0.88 -> 0.74 after the same change. might be thrash from warm affinity moving requests across pods and invalidating local KV shards.

matt: snip from CI flamegraph (truncated):
```
decode_main
 ├─ kv_cache_lookup (20%)
 ├─ attention_transpose_kernel (35%)   <<< unexpected
 ├─ matmul (18%)
 └─ scheduler_select_batch (12%)
```

priya: that attention_transpose jump suggests we're routing different kernels based on sequence-length heuristics? any recent kernel selector logic in that PR?

dan: 4872 adjusts batcher to favor microbatches for lower latency at low QPS by lowering the merge threshold. but it also enabled warm affinity routing which pins requests to warm workers. combo seems to increase small-batch churn and push decode into a kernel path that uses a slower transpose (fallback) for many short seqs.

liu: confirmed: sampled logs show kernel_selector chose attn_transpose_fallback for ~40% of requests post-merge vs ~5% before. traceback shows path: selector -> shortseq_flag=true -> use_transpose_kernel if batch_size < 4.

kira: repro command I used:
```
./tools/bench --model gpt-medium --seq 64 --qps 10 --duration 120 --warmup 30
```
run on same canary image with and without the commit to compare.

matt: proposed mitigations:
- hotfix: revert warm_affinity default (quick revert of 9f2ab4e) to canary and hold rollout
- short-term: raise microbatch merge threshold to reduce small-batch rate
- medium: update kernel_selector to avoid transpose fallback for these shortseq+microbatch combos (likely requires perf test)

priya: agree hotfix first. Dan can you open a revert PR? label: rollback/canary-blocker

dan: opening now. PR #4920 (revert: prefer_warm_affinity default). bumping in review and adding CI run.

liu: I'll run a targeted perf CI with flamegraphs after revert is applied to confirm. also will run a kv-metrics dashboard diff to show hitrate recovery.

kira: add a canary hold flag in rollout pipeline once revert merges. we should prevent auto-promote.

ci-bot: perf job queued: runtime/perf/e2e-p95 (rerun target: canary-with-revert)

matt: timeline: revert PR -> merge in next 15m -> CI perf in ~30m -> if green we unfreeze canary rollout. owners: dan (revert), liu (perf verification), kira (rollout hold). Please ping here with CI link.

priya: also file a follow-up ticket to decouple warm_affinity from microbatch threshold; seems the interaction was not covered by our perf matrix. tagging infra/perf and eng-runtime.

dan: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4920 :revert: prefer_warm_affinity default

matt: thanks. if anyone sees other odd metrics (queueing, GPU utl) drop them here. :thumbsup:
